S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in financial state (e.g., a lot worse or better off than usual)
patient_info.stressor: After a sudden drop in income left Kaitlyn dependent on relatives and irregular help from friends, money became the center of daily conversations that had once revolved around softball, karaoke nights, and DIY plans. Across 1 year and 2 months, she developed a fixed belief tied to the financial setback, and it held firm despite bank statements, explanations from family members, and repeated efforts by friends to walk through the facts with her. The belief became clinically significant when it led to repeated confrontations about bills, community fundraisers, and shared travel plans, straining the social network she usually relied on. She came to psychiatric care through a county clinic after a social services worker helping with financial assistance noticed the persistence of the belief and offered a mental health appointment as part of stabilizing her situation.

S019.name: Delusions

S019.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Other than the arguments about the money, I still handle my own meals, get to the county clinic and assistance appointments, and keep my things in order the same way I always have.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: Because I keep bringing up the money, relatives avoid helping me with bills and friends have stopped including me in fundraisers and travel plans.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on since my income dropped, about a year and two months ago.
